quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #13
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle's right wheels leave the pavement?

options.text: Stop quickly.
Pull completely off the road and get back on when it is safe.
Speed up and steer back onto the road quickly.
Release the accelerator, slow down, then carefully steer back onto the road when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the accelerator, slow down, then carefully steer back onto the road when safe.
questions.explanation: If your right wheels leave the pavement, do not panic. Release the accelerator and steer parallel to the road. Slow down gradually. Keep both hands on the wheel and steer gently back onto the road. Check for traffic before returning to the pavement.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic signal has the same requirements as:

options.text: A slow sign.
A yield sign.
A stop sign.
An intersection sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign.
questions.explanation: At a flashing red signal, you must stop. Then yield to all traffic that does not have to stop.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Lane ends.
No right turn.
Slippery when wet.
Two-way traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lane ends.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow and black. They tell you about upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns that a lane is ending. Be ready to let traffic merge safely.

questions.question: When your line of traffic is crossing railroad tracks with no signals or gates:

options.text: You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains.
You may pass slower drivers while crossing the tracks.
Make sure your vehicle can fully cross the tracks without stopping.
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your vehicle can fully cross the tracks without stopping.
questions.explanation: Before driving onto railroad tracks, check that you have enough space to cross completely without stopping. Never pass another vehicle at a railroad crossing. Always look for trains before crossing any tracks.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a roadway from a private road?

options.text: Honk your horn to warn other cars.
Partially drive onto the roadway to alert other drivers.
Drive out fast to merge smoothly with traffic.
Yield to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway.
questions.explanation: When entering a roadway from a driveway or private road, you must give the right-of-way to pedestrians and all traffic already on the roadway.

questions.question: At a school crossing sign, you should:

options.text: Always stop, even without a stop sign.
Watch for children and be ready to stop.
Always sound your horn when you see children.
Be ready to help children cross the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: Always yield to pedestrians in or entering a crosswalk. Stay alert for pedestrians when driving through intersections or turning.

questions.question: What is the first thing you should adjust when you get into a car to drive?

options.text: Your seat belt
The steering wheel
Your rearview mirror
Your seat

questions.correctAnswerText: Your seat
questions.explanation: First, adjust your seat so you are comfortable and can see the road clearly. After your seat is set, adjust your mirrors and steering wheel.

questions.question: When changing lanes you should not:

options.text: Check your side and rearview mirrors.
Use your turn signal.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.
Use your cell phone to call police about road conditions ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your cell phone to call police about road conditions ahead.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors for traffic behind you. Use your turn signal to let others know your plan. Look for other drivers also moving into your target lane.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you must:

options.text: Slow down and stay in your lane.
Keep driving in your lane.
Pull to the right side and stop.
Stop immediately where you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right side and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing lights or hear a siren from an emergency vehicle, pull to the right side of the road immediately and stop.

questions.question: Your power steering stops working while you are driving. You should:

options.text: Honk your horn and turn off the engine.
Turn on hazard lights and brace yourself.
Steer with extra effort, slow down, drive to a safe area, and stop.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer with extra effort, slow down, drive to a safe area, and stop.
questions.explanation: Without power steering, you need more strength to steer. Slow down gradually and drive to a safe place off the road to stop.

questions.question: You are driving in the right lane of a multilane highway and want to move into the left lane. You should:

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for traffic behind you before changing lanes.
Look over your left shoulder to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes.
Check your side mirror for traffic and turn on your turn signal.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to make sure no vehicles are in the lane you want to enter. Always use your turn signal when changing lanes.

questions.question: If you drink alcohol socially, what helps ensure safe driving?

options.text: Drink coffee before driving.
Get a ride home from a friend who has not been drinking.
Take a cold shower before driving.
Stop drinking 30 minutes before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get a ride home from a friend who has not been drinking.
questions.explanation: The safest way to avoid impaired driving is to arrange a ride with a friend who is not drinking. Coffee and cold showers do not reduce the effects of alcohol. The body needs about one hour to eliminate the alcohol from one drink.

questions.question: Drivers may not park within ____ of a railroad crossing.

options.text: 50 feet
65 feet
100 feet
80 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 50 feet
questions.explanation: Do not park within 50 feet of a railroad crossing. Parking too close can cause crashes.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is approaching.
Look both ways as you cross the intersection.
Always come to a full stop at the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: Slow down as you approach a yield sign. Be ready to stop and let other vehicles and pedestrians go first. You must stop at a yield sign if traffic requires it.

questions.question: As you near an intersection, the traffic light changes from green to yellow. Your best action is to:

options.text: Speed up to pass through before the red light.
Brake hard to stop.
Be ready to stop in the middle of the intersection.
Be ready to stop before the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop before the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the light will soon turn red. Prepare to stop before entering the intersection if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: Which of the following does not happen after drinking?

options.text: Your reflexes and reaction time slow down.
Your judgment of speed and distance becomes unclear.
You are less alert.
You become calm and can concentrate better.

questions.correctAnswerText: You become calm and can concentrate better.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time, reduces your vision, makes it harder to judge speed and distance, reduces recovery from headlight glare, and often makes you more likely to take risks.

questions.question: As a pedestrian, you should:

options.text: Always have the right-of-way over vehicles when using a crosswalk.
Never walk into the street or a crosswalk when vehicles are coming.
Enter a crosswalk anytime because the driver must stop.
Use crosswalks only when convenient.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never walk into the street or a crosswalk when vehicles are coming.
questions.explanation: Do not enter the street or a crosswalk when vehicles are approaching. Even though pedestrians have the right-of-way in crosswalks, a close vehicle may not be able to stop in time.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle on a two-lane road with traffic going both ways, you should:

options.text: Return to your lane when you have enough space between you and the vehicle you passed.
Stay in the left lane if you plan to turn left.
Return to the right side of the road right away.
Drive in either lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Return to your lane when you have enough space between you and the vehicle you passed.
questions.explanation: When passing on a two-lane road, return to the right side once there is enough space between you and the vehicle you passed.

questions.question: Which of the following must you obey over the other three?

options.text: A steady red light
A police officer
A stop sign
A flashing red light

questions.correctAnswerText: A police officer
questions.explanation: Orders from traffic officers take priority over signs, signals, and road markings. Traffic officers include police, fire police, construction zone flag persons, and school crossing guards.

questions.question: What should you do if your accelerator sticks while you are driving?

options.text: Reach down and try to pull it up.
Shift to park.
Shift to neutral and press the brake firmly.
Turn off the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to neutral and press the brake firmly.
questions.explanation: If your accelerator sticks, keep your eyes on the road. Shift to neutral and press the brake firmly. Pull off the road when it is safe and turn off the engine.

questions.question: What happens to your field of vision when you drive faster?

options.text: It gets wider.
It gets narrower.
It makes it easier to see side traffic.
It stays the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gets narrower.
questions.explanation: When you drive faster, your field of vision becomes narrower. As your speed increases, you see less to the sides. You must watch carefully for hazards.

questions.question: Another driver is passing your car. What should you do?

options.text: Pull off the road.
Signal to them when it is safe to pass.
Check for oncoming traffic and slow down to help them pass safely.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for oncoming traffic and slow down to help them pass safely.
questions.explanation: Stay to the right when another driver passes you. Check for oncoming traffic and slow down. This helps them pass safely and return to your lane easily.

questions.question: When driving in fog, what should you do?

options.text: Drive slowly and reduce your speed.
Do not use your high beam headlights.
Use low beam headlights to see the road better.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Fog reduces visibility of vehicles, pedestrians, and traffic signals. Slow down and drive carefully. Do not use high beams. Use low beams instead — they light up the road better in fog.

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle with sirens or flashing lights approaches you, you must:

options.text: Move to the right and stop.
Move to the right and slow down.
Move to the right and turn on your four-way flashers.
Stop and let it pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with lights and sirens, immediately move to the right side of the road and stop.

questions.question: When must you stop for a school bus?

options.text: When it is parked on the shoulder with no one in it.
When it approaches you, even without flashing lights.
When you are on a two-lane road and its red lights are flashing.
Whenever the driver waves at you.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are on a two-lane road and its red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: Stop when a school bus shows flashing red lights while picking up or dropping off children. On a two-lane road, traffic in both directions must stop and stay stopped while the red lights are flashing or the stop arm is extended.

questions.question: Your car hits a parked car and you cannot find the owner. What should you do?

options.text: You have done all you can.
You must wait for the police.
You must leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.
You can leave.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.
questions.explanation: When you hit an unattended car, try to find the owner. If you cannot, leave a written note with your name, address, and details of the accident.

questions.question: What makes a person sober up after drinking alcohol?

options.text: Only time
A cold shower
Eating food
Drinking coffee

questions.correctAnswerText: Only time
questions.explanation: Cold showers, black coffee, or exercise cannot make someone sober. Only time reduces alcohol's effects, based on body weight, number of drinks consumed, and food eaten.

questions.question: If your turn signals do not work, how should you signal that you are turning?

options.text: Use your horn.
Use your headlights.
Use hand signals.
Use your emergency flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use hand signals.
questions.explanation: If your turn signals do not work, use hand signals to tell other drivers you are turning.

questions.question: If your car starts to skid, what should you do?

options.text: Turn the wheel too far the other way.
Turn your wheel toward oncoming traffic.
Turn your wheel in the direction the car is skidding.
Let go of the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheel in the direction the car is skidding.
questions.explanation: If your car skids, stay calm. Steer the wheel in the direction of the skid.

questions.question: When stopped behind a motorcycle, how much distance should you allow?

options.text: At least one full vehicle length.
At least three full vehicle lengths.
At least two feet.
At least four feet.

questions.correctAnswerText: At least one full vehicle length.
questions.explanation: Stop a safe distance behind motorcycles at traffic lights and crossings. A full vehicle length is recommended to prevent a collision if your car is hit from behind. Motorcycles can stop faster than cars in dry conditions, so stay alert.
